text:
sam: Heads up — seeing a spike of GPU pods Pending in eu-west1-prod. Scheduler messages show Fit failures: "node(s) had no available devices" and "0/6 nodes are available: 4 did not match node affinity, 2 insufficient resources". CA doesn't seem to be creating nodes. anyone else?

lina: Yep, noticed this at ~08:10. CA logs show API errors when trying to create nodes: "quotaExceeded: IN_USE_ADDRESSES" from cloud provider. New nodes fail during NIC allocation.

maria: Also odd packing behavior — a bunch of pods request fractional GPUs `nvidia.com/gpu: 0.5`. Our device plugin/driver mix is MIG on some pools, non-MIG on others. fractional requests + mixed node types = scheduler placing 1 pod/node often.

neil: Can you paste a failing pod spec?

sam: here's the relevant part from one pending pod:
```yaml
metadata:
  name: model-infer-5cdf
spec:
  containers:
  - name: worker
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: "2000m"
        memory: "8Gi"
        nvidia.com/gpu: "0.5"
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: "0.5"
```

lina: That explains a lot. k8s device plugin treats any positive GPU request as "needs a whole device" unless the device plugin and node support MIG slicing and advertise fractional resources. Our g4dn nodepool does not.

maria: Related config: `nodePool/gpu-max-pods` was lowered last week to 8 to reduce `maxPods` per node (we noticed network pressure). That plus the fractional requests means we end up with poor binpacking. CA can't consolidate because even empty nodes count toward quota and IPs.

ops-bot: deploy-bot reports: ERROR creating nodepool-eu-west1-gpu: quotaExceeded: IN_USE_ADDRESSES. (request id: fd3a-9c1)

neil: So two root causes colliding: (1) cloud external IPs exhausted -> CA create-node failing, (2) fractional GPU requests with a mixed node fleet -> scheduler poor fit.

lina: Short-term mitigations:
- set a mutating webhook to rewrite `nvidia.com/gpu: 0.5` -> `1` for non-MIG pools (quick and dirty)
- scale down some non-critical services into a spot-only pool to free IPs
- request IN_USE_ADDRESSES quota bump for eu-west1

maria: Longer term: consolidate to a MIG-first pool (annotate nodes `gpu.mig=true`) and add admission logic that matches pod annotation `gpu.slice=true`. Also revisit the `maxPods` tuning (it was reactive).

sam: I started a short-lived workaround: created taint `gpu:fractional=true:NoSchedule` on non-MIG nodes and added toleration to the pods pinned to MIG. That helped pack 3 pods per MIG node.

neil: Nice. For the autoscaler, we should also change scale-up to fallback to a different zone where IPs are available if eu-west1 is exhausted. CA does support fallback in our fork.

lina: Filed infra ticket: https://redwood.atlas/ops/INC-4821 (requesting IP quota + temporary secondary-subnet expansion).

maria: I'll open an RFC to standardize GPU request semantics (MIG vs non-MIG) and propose a mutating webhook approach for the interim.

sam: I'll also add a dashboard alert for "node creation failures due to IP quota" so ops sees this before pods pile up.

neil: :thumbsup:

maria: tagging @cloud-sre for quota follow-up.

lina: Summary: immediate actions = quota request + webhook tweak + evacuate low-priority pods; medium = create MIG pool + admission annotations; long = infra RFC and autoscaler fallback config.

sam: thanks all — I'll send a brief to oncall and update the incident channel if things change.
